metadata.title: Logix computer sales and Academy demand through NCC 1980
metadata.status: Alternative-history planning forecast; not actual sales, firm orders or statistically calibrated probabilities.
metadata.calendar_period: 1978-01-01 to 1978-12-31; no pre-launch Aurelia sales, June–December shown
metadata.launch_year_period: 1978-06-05 to 1979-05-31; rounded planning proxy for sales by June 4 NCC 1979; June 1–3 omitted

reaction_policy.boundary: June 1978–May 1979 sell-through. The June 4 demonstration, October Tandy release, later Apple successor review and confidential July/December IBM actions add no pre-NCC shipments.
reaction_policy.interpretation: Replace the prior generic competitor-response allowance with explicit incremental deviations. Apple losses are transfers to competitor sales; Tandy waiting is deferral beyond cutoff, not shipped Model II units; compatibility confidence is a small positive effect. These are assumptions, not measured elasticities.
reaction_policy.later_tandy_economics: Customer release October 1979; OEM prices and volume not yet forecast. No unsupported incremental Abacus revenue added to current totals.
reaction_policy.bpi_effect: Incremental to already available BPI software: better presentation, demonstrations, training and installation support. Central +1,200 Aurelias; existing positive multipliers give +600/+1,200/+1,800. No double counting of BPI installations as computers; capacity still applies.

assumptions.demand: 22,000 baseline launch-year sales × (revised complete-package price / old price)^(-elasticity), rounded to 1,000 and capped at the scenario delivery capacity, then adjusted by explicit dated competitor/partner effects in market_reactions.json. BPI gains are limited to remaining scenario delivery capacity, with excess demand shown as deferred. Elasticities are judgement assumptions, not historical measurements.
assumptions.monthly_ramp: Monthly weights are a production/distribution planning allocation, not measured seasonality. Prices held at June 1978 snapshot through May 1979; no use of June 1979 prices before NCC.
assumptions.market_denominator: 180,000 US calendar-1978 purchases without Logix and 250,000 launch-year purchases without Logix are modelling assumptions, not sourced historical counts. Different periods must not be mixed. New/accelerated purchases plus competitor halo expand the denominator; diverted purchases do not.
assumptions.mix: 80% Office grayscale bundle; 20% colour system plus separately purchased Business Tools and Abacus. One disk per computer, 70% printer attachment. All sales use baseline 25% dealer fee; no extra direct-sales margin is assumed.
assumptions.accounting: Customer retail spend is not manufacturer revenue. Supplier revenue combines Logix/AION offering receipts after channel fees; legal-entity allocation is not modelled. Contribution excludes campaign, Academy setup, credits, R&D, capital, finance and tax. Academy tuition revenue is excluded. BPI licence receipts are separately reported and excluded from Logix/AION totals; neither BPI specialist support costs nor corporate profit are estimated.
assumptions.production: Central case needs about 4,920 monthly customer deliveries by May 1979 plus demonstration/service/inventory stock. Existing manufacturing costs assume 10,000 annual units per hardware family and are held unchanged, not treated as proof of capacity or automatic scale savings.
assumptions.marketing: Assumes qualified launch software, effective dealer demonstrations and campaign delivery. Free TV packages do not imply guaranteed airtime. Incremental Apple, public Tandy-announcement and compatibility-confidence effects are explicitly tabulated; private cooperation and later IBM actions have no early demand effect.
assumptions.uncertainty: Central estimate is a planning case. Demand response, manufacturing yield, disk/printer supply, channel reach and service quality dominate uncertainty.

bpi_policy.scope: 15/20/25% first-purchase attachment; scenario assumptions, not observed conversions. Existing BPI availability is already in baseline; only stronger execution adds hardware demand.
bpi_policy.mix: 50% accounting-only, 25% four-module trading configuration, 25% complete suite; rounded per month. A suite is one licence entitlement covering five modules.
bpi_policy.ownership: BPI receipts belong to independent BPI Systems; not Logix/AION revenue or Adam personal income.
bpi_policy.exclusions: No Tandy BPI port, training, setup fees, support profit, equity income or upgrade revenue forecast. Upgrade credits are not hidden inside first-purchase cohorts. No extra RAM/drive sales assumed before configuration qualification.
bpi_policy.capacity: Use existing delivery caps; strong-case BPI demand above capacity is deferred beyond cutoff. Academy BPI enrolments are part of existing 10,000–13,000 capacity, not extra hardware sales.

academy.gates: Expand after sustained 70–75% classroom occupancy or two-week waiting lists; use dealer-hosted/visiting classes before a permanent lease. Enrolments include repeat students, not additional computer sales. Target assumes eight learners per room and advance instructor recruitment.
academy.status: Recommended central-scenario capacity roadmap, not approved city selections or actual openings.

context_sources.title: Contemporary BYTE report of Dataquest 1978 market estimates
context_sources.use: Historical scale context only; not the numerical US denominators above.

context_sources.title: Dan Bricklin: VisiCalc release history
context_sources.use: October 1979 release context for the earlier Abacus business proposition; not demand-elasticity evidence.

post_ncc_policy.period: 1979-06-01 through 1979-11-30; no Aurelia+ deliveries before its canonical 1979-12-03 launch
post_ncc_policy.price_basis: Use June 15 annual pricing snapshots as proxies for NCC June 4 prices. June has 3/30 old-price and 27/30 new-price exposure, assuming uniform daily purchases. Later months use 1979 prices. This is an explicit timing assumption, not a new catalog price announcement.
post_ncc_policy.baseline: Each scenario starts from its May delivered run rate, which already includes established Abacus, BPI, Academy, advertising and existing competition. Monthly factors model channel maturation and autumn buying. They are judgement inputs, not observed seasonality or a second launch-year price uplift.
post_ncc_policy.effect_boundaries: Rates are additive increments against price-adjusted demand, not measured conversions. Campaign covers NCC and July roadshows; BPI covers additional independent sales/support execution; ecosystem confidence covers interoperability and third-party peripheral availability. Existing benefits remain in the May base. Tandy waiting starts with its public demonstration; the October customer release increases substitution. Apple native cards may help competitors. No unsigned OEM contract, partner computer shipment, BPI Tandy port, IBM-delay windfall or future architecture detail is assumed.
post_ncc_policy.successor: No unannounced Aurelia+ specification, price or launch-date knowledge is assigned to 1979 buyers. Generic migration uncertainty is modelled; successor-announcement deferral would require a dated public event. November Aurelia+ sales are zero.
post_ncc_policy.backlog: Only explicitly tracked BPI capacity-deferred demand opens June. Each month 75% of prior unmet demand retries; 25% lapses. New demand plus retries is capped by delivery capacity; unmet demand is neither a sale nor a firm order. Other untracked pre-June lost demand is not invented.
post_ncc_policy.capacity_status: Assumed net customer delivery ceilings, not funded production commitments. Central November capacity of 7,200 is 46% above May deliveries; factory, disks, printers, working capital, service stock and dealer readiness must support it. No automatic cost savings are taken.
post_ncc_policy.market_scope: Forecast Logix Aurelia customer purchases only. Competing compatible computers and third-party peripherals are not Logix sales. OEM royalties, expansion-card sales to other installed bases, standalone software and Academy receipts remain unquantified; no extended-period market share is asserted without a new denominator.

ncc1980_policy.period: 1979-12-01 to 1980-05-18 inclusive; May 1–18 only, before the NCC launch
ncc1980_policy.price_basis: Hold existing products at June 1979 prices and costs. New COMDEX products use their first available June 1980 snapshots as provisional launch-period price/cost proxies, not proof of December quotes. Do not apply a June 1980 price cut to existing products before NCC. Financial estimates require sensitivity review once launch quotes exist.
ncc1980_policy.baseline: Use November new demand, already including the June price response and NCC campaign. Add only incremental COMDEX/product/workshop effects. No new universal price cut or quantified speed claim.
ncc1980_policy.plus_price_response: Preference shares precede price response. Apply (Plus average package / retained Aurelia average package)^(-scenario elasticity) to the Plus-intending cohort; the premium deters some purchases rather than silently assuming willingness to pay. COMDEX application gains already represent feature benefits; no extra quality multiplier. Existing-price Aurelia intentions are unchanged.
ncc1980_policy.capacity: Assumed net customer-delivery ceilings and product-specific ramp, not proven factory capacity. No model is forced to retire. Do not move unfilled old-model requests into Plus without modelling a buyer decision. Unused capacity is not a sale.
ncc1980_policy.timing: December Plus demand/capacity exposure is 29/31 because launch is December 3. May demand and capacity are 18/31 of a month. Monthly rows are approximations, not dated individual orders.
ncc1980_policy.backlog: 75% of each model’s opening unmet demand retries; 25% lapses. November backlog opens as Aurelia demand. Separate product queues; no automatic substitution. Fresh demand plus returning demand equals deliveries plus ending unmet demand.
ncc1980_policy.competition: Independent ports/clones gain gradually after kit availability; this is a substitution sensitivity, not named OEM shipment evidence. Other manufacturers’ systems and royalties remain outside Logix computer totals. No next-generation details or post-NCC hardware sales enter the forecast.
ncc1980_policy.application_upgrades: Existing November Aurelia cohort only: monthly Abacus 2 full-licence purchase assumptions 2/2.5/2.5/2/1.5/1.5% before scenario scaling and partial-month exposure. No unapproved upgrade discount. These licences are separate from new-machine bundle licences; Pulse attached to new Aurelia+ systems only is reported separately.
ncc1980_policy.scope: All forecasts are US scenario sell-through. Academy attendance is a consequence/channel interaction already reflected in demand, not another additive computer-sales uplift. No new market-share denominator or corporate-profit claim.

academy_demand_policy.period: June 1979–May 18, 1980; prospective demand/capacity extension of the original first-year roadmap
academy_demand_policy.unit: Course enrolments, not unique people, graduations or additional computer purchases. Repeat attendance across courses/months is allowed; no unique-student count is inferred.
academy_demand_policy.drivers: New-system customers, owners of the installed base, prospective buyers who do not buy in that month, and manufacturer/integrator learners. These are enrolment requests; no extra hardware conversion bonus is added.
academy_demand_policy.course_mapping: Use the existing 2/5/6/5-day courses; charts/layouts enter Abacus teaching after December 3. BPI uses 3-day and Pulse 2-day planning allowances already in the cost model. Manufacturer learners consume developer capacity; optional engineering subscriptions are not course enrolments.
academy_demand_policy.staffing: Plan 1.25 instructors per room, including specialist capability; room-days are capped by both rooms and instructors. Cross-trained BPI/Pulse teachers and geographic fit remain hiring/scheduling gates. Counts are aggregate capacity targets, not signed leases or named openings.
academy_demand_policy.capacity: Plan classes at six occupied seats (75% of eight). Reserve whole class blocks by course duration; demand is allocated proportionally, then capped by requested places. May uses 18/31 of room/instructor days; December Pulse classes begin only after launch. No course starting too late to finish by cutoff is assumed.
academy_demand_policy.backlog: 75% of unmet enrolment requests retry the following period; 25% lapse. Capacity is measured in teaching days, so a five-day course consumes more than Fundamentals.
academy_demand_policy.accounting: Tuition, support costs and purchase-credit redemption are not quantified here. Existing 50% Fundamentals credit and six-month expiry remain; other eligible course vouchers retain their terms. Student attendance is not a second computer purchase.
academy_demand_policy.previous_period: The original 10,000–13,000 first-year enrolment target is retained, not presented as actual attendance. No historical enrolments are fabricated to reconcile it.
